correctness.rationale: The finite-N identity p_N=E exp[-a(log N)^2/Y_(N)] follows from Y_i=t0/tau_i ~ Gamma(1/2,1) and a single shared exponential clock. Uniform exponential moments of the centered Gamma maximum below a=1 give Gamma(1-a)(pi log N)^(-a/2) N^(-a). At and above a=1, the exactly normalized tilted density exp[-y-aL^2/y]/sqrt(pi y) has center sqrt(a)L and CLT variance sqrt(a)L/2; the transition factor crosses at y=L+O(log L), proving 1/2 at a=1, N^(1-2sqrt(a)) for a>1 and Phi(z/sqrt(2)) in a_N=1+z/sqrt(L). Renewal Laplace transform then gives r_N p_N T_N=>Exp(1) and exact E T_N=(1-p_N)/(r_N p_N). Independently integrated both exact finite-N formulas at (N,a)=(2,.5),(4,1),(12,2) and found agreement. Checked restrictions N>=2, fixed positive a, d,D>0, and fixed-z crossover; no a=0 or uniform-z conclusion.
residual_risks: No infinite-N limit is certified by finite quadrature; the tilted-CLT and uniform integrability arguments are essential.
